I am absolutely astonished at how ugly this movie is. I complained that the 2005 one had lots of bad CG, but oh my god it’s maybe even worse here almost two decades later and there’s wayyyy more of it just constantly. It’s so bad that I was genuinely wondering at times if some of the effects were AI generated. Amidst all the bad greenscreen and CGI is the occasional physical prop or set, which look so cheap you’d think these specialized props were purchased at Spirit Halloween. And as if that’s not bad enough, the whole movie has this gross filter that takes all the color out and makes it look gray and dull and terrible. I hate it I hate it I hate it, not one fucking frame of this movie looks even somewhat okay to the point that it made me actually angry while watching. I could genuinely complain about it so much more, I would rate this at least a full star higher if it wasn’t one of the ugliest movies I’ve ever seen in my entire life. The plot of this movie is real basic and predictable but not bad. The cast is all pretty good, I was not really expecting to like Timothee Chalamet as Wonka but I honestly did. There’s some good music but some of the songs are kinda boring and go on longer than they need to. The humor is mixed with some genuinely funny jokes and some really obnoxious bad comedy. As dumb and nostalgia bait-y as he was, I also kinda liked the Oompa Loompa. Real shame about the entire look of every single thing tho.

Le film de Paul King sur le biopic de Wonka est une oeuvre orienté jeunesse. On sens une très grande inspiration cartoon de NOS jeunes années. Les chansons et danses omniprésentes parlent d'eux même mais ne sont pas les seuls points caractérisant ce coté cartoons. Les cadrages et décors colorés rappellent des prises de vue non habituelle du cinéma et une autre facon de retourner dans notre enfance. Le scénario va de paire avec cette idée, pas très elaboré ni très originale, cependant efficace. Le seul point noir de ce film est sa pâte graphique. Quelques manques de qualité de 3D se font ressentir. Surtout lors de deux scenes, les bonbons volants et la scène final de la fabrique. Malgré tout la girafe CGI fait très bien son effet. C'est avec plaisir que j'ai vu ce film de Paul King qui m'a encore renvoyé en enfance après ma découverte de ce réalisateur avec les deux films Paddington qui m'ont émerveillé.

“This film could have been delicious but it blows up bigger than Violet Beauregarde. Timothee Chalamet does his best Gene Wilder impression but his over acting throughout is just cringeworthy and fails to capture the charm of Wilder’s Wonka portrayal. For a musical, the songs are just bad and unmemorable; rhyming chocolate with anything by putting ‘oco-late’ on the end is just lazy writing. It also doesn’t matter how many great British actors from Peep Show and Horrible Histories you shove in, none of them could save this mess, instead making it even worse with the sheer number just adding to the ridiculousness of the film. (How and why is Phil Wang even in this?!) Verdict: This makes the Tim Burton film look good.

❝ we are the music makers, and we are the dreamers of dreams. ❞ wonka felt like walking through a sweet shop at christmas — warm lights, colourful wrappers, and the smell of chocolate drifting through the air before you’ve even stepped inside. i went into it expecting something whimsical, and it certainly has that storybook charm. the film moves with a kind of cheerful optimism that feels very disney-coded, as though the world might become kinder if everyone sang at the right moment and shared a piece of chocolate. timothée chalamet brings a gentle sweetness to wonka that makes him easy to root for. this version of the character feels less eccentric genius and more hopeful dreamer, which gives the film a softer, more fairy-tale quality. what i enjoyed most was the atmosphere. there are moments that genuinely feel magical — little bursts of colour and wonder that reminded me of opening a childhood book and finding illustrations tucked between the pages. at the same time, i found myself wanting a little more of the strange edge that makes willy wonka such a fascinating character. the film is so determined to be charming that it occasionally feels a bit too safe, and some of the magic slips through my fingers before it can fully settle. still, there’s something comforting about it. it feels like a rainy-afternoon film: cosy, sugary, and easy to spend time with, even if it didn’t completely enchant me. a sweet, whimsical adventure that made me smile, even if it never quite became the golden-ticket experience i hoped for.

Wonka is exactly what I need a tale from the mind of the wonderful Roald Dahl to be, a delightfully fun and whimsical romp with a bit of fun and heart to it, I was obsessed with Roald Dahl books growing up, yet Wonka never took my fancy as a film, I’m not sure if it’s because I’m not a massive musicals guy, or just because I was more of a fan of works like The Twits growing up, but if this wasn’t put on in work it probably wouldn’t of been one I was watching any time soon, However within a minute of this being put on I was hooked, drawn to the screen by the energetic performance of Timothée Chalamet, he’s probably my favourite young actor today and he brings to life the energy and charisma of Willy Wonka just like those who have come before, it’s not just Chalamet who holds up his end of the bargain either, everyone holds there own in this film through there magical performances and looking a the cast list it’s not hard to see why, but as a Brit who loves Peep Show I’ve got to give a special mention to Paterson Joseph, his role as Johnson is my favourite in Peep Show, he’s electric in every role I’ve seen him in and often steals the show, he goes toe to toe with the eccentric Wonka as the evil businessman Slugworth and I’d be lying if there both not as good as each other here, But even if the performances and whimsical world of Roald Dahl isn’t enough to sell you this movie breezes by you with its fun nature, I said to the people in work it boils down really to a serious crime/thriller movie for families, Wonka trying to take and supply on the Businessmen Turf , the evil Businessmen trying to take down the honourable man, but it’s set in the world of Wonka , so it’s fun whimsical and a really enjoyable time for all ages, Wonka is a extremely fun time filled with great music and perfectly capturing the spirit and childhood imagination that all good Roald Dahl stories/worlds have, Chalamet oozes out the seems in the role of Wonka and it would be a crime if we never got to see him portray the role again, the rest of the cast hold there own and it wears its heart and emotions on it sleeves, colourful and dreamy yet serious when it needs to be, Wonka is a fun time that never feels like it outstays its welcome for to long and if your a fan of the Willy Wonka character or any other Dahl’s works, you won’t be left feeling disappointed

‘Tis the season for a sweet treat and, whilst not anything to do with Christmas, Wonka hits quite a lot of the festive buttons: fun, light-hearted, colourful and one for all the family. With much of the Paddington team behind this, it delivers that quintessentially English, quirky family film that its forebear (pun intended) achieved but sprinkled with a little bit of Cruella in its prequel backstory to a familiar character. It doesn’t present the titular chocolatier as a villain though, and rubs maybe just a little too much mystery off of the character, but does still feel very much a Roald Dahl tale. Wonka’s dream is to open a chocolate shop and he arrives in an alt-Paris (I think it’s meant to be Paris) to compete against the most famous chocolate makers of the time. From there, frolics, mishaps and big musical numbers ensue. Yes, this is a full musical like the OG Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory. Taking a couple of the songs but throwing in some excellent originals, this could well be destined for a stage run itself in the future. It’s cut through with a particularly English sense of humour and a brilliant ‘spot the famous person’ cast with a, hopefully intended, hat tip to Peep Show and yet another turn from Hugh Grant’s new comedy persona as an Oompa-Loompa. It’s just an utter delight, against all the odds, much like the aforementioned Cruella. A brisk and breezy one-for-all-the-family movie to smack a smile on your face. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
